newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Krakow to issue PLN 55 mln munibonds.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Krakow to issue PLN 55 mln munibonds.

text.p: The southern Polish city of Krakow plans to issue municipal bonds worth 55 million zlotys in 1997, the Krakow municipality treasurer said on Tuesday.

"The bonds will be sold in two tranches -- the first will be worth 25 million zlotys and mature in ten years and the second...up to 30 million zlotys and will mature in nine years," Leslaw Fijal told Reuters.
He said the issues would be closed and directed to up to 300 investors. The city authorities will discuss details of the issue in the next few days, he added. @
The funds raised by the issue will be used to build a fast tramway route and repair road pavement, Fijal said.
Krakow deputy president Krzysztof Goerlich has said his municipality was considering issuing bonds to foreign investors in 1998.
Last year Krakow sold five-year floating rate bonds worth 15 million zlotys, its first ever bond issue.
